file.summary: Frasers, which already owned 22.90% of Accent, has been standing in the market since 15 June 2026 offering A$0.65 cash for every share, with sellers paid two trading days after they sell. This isn't a normal takeover: Frasers' own Bidder's Statement says the aim is to reach at least 26%, which under its 2025 subscription agreement lets it ask for a second board seat, and it "does not expect to achieve more than 90%". The bid drew almost no sellers until Frasers declared the price best and final on 28 October, after which it bought about 5.9 million shares in two days and now sits at 23.94%. Compulsory acquisition (90%) is far out of reach, Accent's board says reject, and the shares closed at A$0.655 on 30 October, above the bid, so there's no spread to capture: the bid works as a floor at A$0.65 until 29 January 2027 rather than as a deal that pays out. The event that matters next is the 20 November AGM and possible board spill, where Frasers' extra votes count.

- Price: fixed at A$0.65 and declared BEST AND FINAL, WILL NOT BE INCREASED (Frasers, 28 Oct 2026). Frasers is held to that statement, so this bid can't be raised.
- Withdrawal: Frasers "reserves the right to withdraw unaccepted Offers in the circumstances permitted by, and in accordance with, Part 6.7 of the Corporations Act" (Barrenjoey, 15 Jun 2026). Nothing suggests it intends to.

file.risks:
For a holder the question isn't "will the deal complete" but "will the A$0.65 floor still be there when I want to use it", and "is there any upside above A$0.65".
- Bid withdrawn before 29 Jan 2027: under 5%. Withdrawal is only allowed in the narrow cases Part 6.7 permits, and Frasers is buying at the price it wants. Would rise if something drastic happened at Accent (for example, a large share issue).
- Offer simply lapses on 29 Jan 2027 and the price falls: the main risk for anyone holding above A$0.65. Frasers says the price "may fall after the close of the Offer". Accent shares have closed between A$0.65 and A$0.66 since 7 Oct 2026 (Frasers, 28 Oct), which suggests the bid is holding the price up. Would worsen if Accent's trading stays weak (two FY26 earnings downgrades, per the Bidder's Statement).
- Compulsory acquisition at 90%: under 2%. Frasers needs about 397 million more shares (66% of the company) against a board recommending rejection, and says it doesn't expect to get there.
- Frasers reaching 26%: needs about 12.4 million more shares (2.06%). After the best and final announcement it bought 5.89 million in two days, so this looks reachable before 29 Jan 2027, possibly before the 20 Nov AGM. This doesn't help sellers directly, but it would strengthen Frasers' hand on board seats.
- AGM on 20 Nov 2026: Frasers voted against the 2025 remuneration report (first strike). A second strike would trigger a spill vote. Board turmoil could push the share price either way; it doesn't change the bid terms.

Competing bid prospects (good for holders, kept separate):
- Low, around 5%. Frasers' 23.94% lets it block any scheme (a scheme needs 75% of votes cast) and, after declaring best and final, it can't respond by raising this bid. The IBC has not announced a sale process or any approach. Frasers says no competing proposal has emerged in over four months. A rival would need Frasers to sell to it.

Warburg Pincus (now at A$5.45 plus up to 5 cents of distribution, A$5.50 total) and AVID Property Group (A$5.35 plus 5 cents) are competing for Ingenia, and both proposals are conditional on Ingenia terminating the Peet deal. The Peet timetable also appears to have stalled: the first court hearing targeted for late October has not been announced, and Peet's 30 October business update reads like a standalone company, saying nothing about the scheme. Peet closed at A$1.42 on 30 October against a paper value of about A$2.47, which says the market thinks the deal is unlikely to complete.

desk_log.head: 2026-11-01, Undisturbed dates filled for every live deal; Peet's undisturbed price moved to 9 Jul
desk_log.body:
The break price moves the undisturbed price with the market from its own date, so each live deal
now has that date, from the deal database's undisturbed basis: BET 7 Aug, OML 28 Apr (before the
first proposal), AUC 14 Aug, SDF 9 Jun (before the NBIO), MEI 30 Sep, CWY 12 Aug (before the NBIO)
and FPR 31 Jul (before SG Fleet's approach). PPC: A$1.81 (21 Aug) to A$1.70, the close on 9 Jul,
the undisturbed date Peet's own presentation uses, before the first approach on 10 Jul. AX1 has no
break price (an unconditional on-market bid). From the independent review of 1 Nov, finding 4.

desk_log.head: 2026-11-01, Deals added from the sweep: A11 and GL1; NZX has none live
desk_log.body:
From the sweep of ASX and NZX announcements (deal files A11.md, GL1.md):
- A11 (Atlantic Lithium, Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt): US$0.25486 cash. Undisturbed A$0.280, the last
  close before the 7 May announcement. Payment indicated only as December 2026, so set to 31 Dec.
- GL1 (Global Lithium, Titan Australia Mining): A$1.15 cash. Undisturbed A$0.665, the last close
  before the 22 Sep announcement. Payment indicated as mid-January 2027, so set to 15 Jan.
- Not added: RCT (Reef Casino Trust; Iris already holds 96.5% and will compulsorily acquire; only
  the payment is left), and EUR and CNB (both effective, paying in early November).
- NZX: no live control deal at NZ$20m or more. Bremworth and 2 Cheap Cars have finished. Watching
  non-binding approaches: thl (update by the 6 Nov AGM), SkyCity (structured process since 30 Sep).
Both new deals have no stored prices yet; the nightly fetch adds them.

- RTH: dated 16 Oct 2026, the last close before the announcement.

desk_log.head: 2026-11-01, Deal files from primary sources for every live ASX deal; terms corrected
desk_log.body:
The deal files in research/deals/ (one per live deal, from the announcements, booklets, deeds, expert
reports and regulators' registers) were folded into config/live_deals.csv with src/deal_files.py.
Terms changed on the live list, each from its deal file:
- VAU: cash A$0.475 to A$0.5125 a share, raised to make up for the Genesis A$0.05 dividend Vault
  holders don't receive (VAU.md, scheme booklet).
- OML: A$1.70 to A$1.68; the 2c interim dividend in the headline was paid on 17 Sep, so a buyer now
  gets A$1.68 (OML.md). Payment moved to 10 Dec after the 30 Oct timetable change.
- AUC: valued as the mix a holder gets if every holder elects cash: A$0.3395 cash plus 0.02525
  OceanaGold shares (NYSE OGC), from the A$194m cash cap over the scheme shares (AUC.md). The old row
  used the A$1.36 cash alternative before scale-back, which overstated the gap to the offer
  (12.9% shown; about nil on the mix). OceanaGold added to the nightly fetch as US:OGC.
- SDF: A$6.00 to A$5.8725; the 12.75c FY26 dividend was paid on 25 Sep (SDF.md).
- PPC: cash A$0.745 to A$0.68; the 6.5c dividend was paid on 22 Sep (PPC.md). The scrip leg is
  still valued at Ingenia's price, which carries the bids for Ingenia itself; the deal file sets
  out why that value disappears if this deal goes ahead.
- Notes rewritten for AX1, BET, RWC, MEI, CWY and FPR from their files.
Added: RTH (Racing and Sports, PA Media scheme at A$1.04 cash), with its undisturbed price of
A$0.54 (the close on 16 Oct). Not added: EUR and CNB, both unconditional and paying in early
November, so only the payment is left.
